assertion_analysis.condition_to_fail: The classifer classifies the capacity refusal as until-changed, which is exactly what reverting 7e68c4f719 restores; the arm is shown red at EXIT=1 in logs/negative-control-capacity-refusal.log.
retry_at is stamped from the pass start or from the hold rather than from the failure moment, so the 30-second difference stops holding; reverting the moment=_now() argument reddens it.
The second pass past the back-off does not reach the launch, which is the held-until-changed behaviour; probe.attempted would stay at one entry.

The later overlapping request is refused and put back with a failure and a retry instant instead of held on the claim, which is what restoring the pre-check does; I measured the base arm red on this test at 509b754be2 and green at head 6f0704c032.
The verdict row no longer records held-on-claim or stops naming the holding run, so the detail loses earlier_id.
The later request fails to launch on the pass two minutes after start, which happens if a back-off was recorded despite the hold.

findings.text: non-blocking: _capacity_refusal() hand-composes the capacity refusal's sentence inside the test rather than taking it from the production emitter (reckon/crew/dispatch_admission.py:271-282 composes it as format_refusal('D09', summary.bound_refusal_text(...))), so the classifier's dependence on that remedy surviving in the refusal text is guarded by a fixture and not by the code. If the D09 wrapping at dispatch_admission.py:274 were dropped, queue_admission.py:940 would classify a capacity refusal as until-changed again and this file would stay green; one assertion over the real emitter's text would close it.
